u3-l01.title: The fork
u3-l01.summary: One piece attacks two at once

u3-l01-s01.text: A fork is one piece attacking two at once: your opponent can only save one. Here the knight checks the king and attacks the queen.

u3-l01-s02.text: Pawns can fork too. When it advances, this pawn attacks the rook and the knight: one of them will be lost.

u3-l01-s03.prompt: Fork with the knight: attack the king and the rook.
u3-l01-s03.hint: Find the square from which the knight attacks g8 and e8 at once.
u3-l01-s03.success: Correct. Nf6+ gives check and attacks the rook: after the check, you capture it.

u3-l01-s04.prompt: Knights aren't the only forking pieces: find one with the bishop.
u3-l01-s04.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u3-l01-s04.hint: Look for a bishop check that, on the same diagonal or the other one, attacks a big piece.

u3-l01-s05.prompt: Advance the pawn to attack two pieces at once.
u3-l01-s05.hint: Pawns capture diagonally: find where it attacks both pieces.
u3-l01-s05.success: Correct. The pawn attacks the rook and the knight.

u3-l01-s06.prompt: Fork with the queen: check the king and attack the rook.
u3-l01-s06.hint: Look for a check on the king's diagonal that also attacks, along a diagonal, the rook on b7.
u3-l01-s06.success: Correct. Qd5+ gives check and attacks the rook on b7.

u3-l01-s07.prompt: Win the queen with a fork. After the check, capture it.
u3-l01-s07.success: Correct. Ne7+ and, when the king moves, Nxc8: you won the queen.
u3-l01-s07.hint: Look for a knight check that also attacks the queen on c8.

u3-l01-s08.prompt: From which square does the knight attack both black rooks?
u3-l01-s08.explanation: From f7, the knight attacks d8 and h8: that forks both rooks.
feedback: From e6 the knight attacks d8, but not h8.
From g6 the knight attacks h8, but not d8.

u3-l01-s09.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u3-l01-s09.hint: Look for a move that attacks two pieces at once, ideally with one of them the king.

u3-l01-s10.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u3-l01-s10.hint: Look for a move that attacks two pieces at once, ideally with one of them the king.

u3-l02-s01.text: The knight can't move: if it did, the bishop would be giving check to the king. It's pinned. When the king is behind it, that's an absolute pin.

u3-l02-s02.text: If the queen is behind it, that's a relative pin: the knight can move, but the bishop would capture the queen.

u3-l02-s03.prompt: Can the black knight on c6 move?
options: No, it's pinned to the king
u3-l02-s03.explanation: The bishop on b5 points at the king on e8 through the knight: if the knight moves, the king is in check.
feedback: Look at the diagonal of the bishop on b5: what's behind the knight?

u3-l02-s04.prompt: Pin the knight on c6 to the king with your bishop.
u3-l02-s04.hint: The bishop on f1 can get onto the diagonal that connects the knight and the king.
u3-l02-s04.success: Correct. Bb5 pins the knight: it can't move without leaving the king in check.

u3-l02-s05.prompt: Pin the queen to the king and win it.
u3-l02-s05.hint: The black queen and king are on the same diagonal. Put your bishop on it, protected by the pawn.
u3-l02-s05.success: Correct. Bd4 pins the queen: if it captures the bishop, the pawn captures the queen.

u3-l02-s06.prompt: The knight on f6 is pinned to the queen. Attack it with a pawn.
u3-l02-s06.hint: A pawn can attack the knight: since it's pinned, moving it is a bad idea.
u3-l02-s06.success: Correct. The knight can't escape without giving up the queen: you win a piece.

u3-l02-s07.prompt: Is this pin absolute or relative?
options: Absolute: the king is behind it
Relative: the queen is behind it
u3-l02-s07.explanation: The queen is behind the knight, not the king: the knight can move, but the queen would be lost.
feedback: Look at which piece is behind the knight, on the bishop's diagonal.

u3-l02-s08.text: To defend against a pin, protect the pinned piece, put another piece in between, or move the king or queen off the line. Here Be7 cuts the diagonal and the knight is free again.

u3-l02-s09.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u3-l02-s09.hint: Look for a piece that can't move because the king or queen is behind it.

u3-l02-s10.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.

u3-l03.title: The discovered attack
u3-l03.summary: One piece steps aside and uncovers another

u3-l03-s01.text: In a discovered attack, one piece moves and uncovers the attack of the piece behind it. Here the bishop gives check and, at the same time, the rook attacks the queen.

u3-l03-s02.prompt: Move the knight with check and win the queen.
u3-l03-s02.hint: If the knight leaves e4 with check, the rook attacks the queen and there's no time to save it.
u3-l03-s02.success: Correct. Nf6+ gives check and uncovers the rook's attack on the queen.

u3-l03-s03.prompt: Advance a pawn with check: as it moves, it uncovers your bishop's attack.
u3-l03-s03.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u3-l03-s03.hint: The pawn in front of your bishop can give check by advancing.

u3-l03-s04.prompt: Which white piece do you have to move so the rook attacks the queen?
u3-l03-s04.explanation: The bishop is blocking the e-file: when it moves, the rook attacks the queen.
feedback: The rook is already on the file: another piece is blocking it.
The king isn't on the e-file.

u3-l03-s05.prompt: Tap the white piece that, when it moves, discovers an attack on the black queen.
u3-l03-s05.hint: Look at the a-file: one of your pieces is between the rook and the queen.

u3-l03-s06.prompt: Give a discovered check with the bishop and win the queen.
u3-l03-s06.success: Correct. Bf5+ and then Bxc8: the rook's check left no time to save the queen.
u3-l03-s06.hint: The bishop can move away with a discovered check and attack the queen on c8 at the same time.

u3-l03-s07.text: To find discovered attacks, look for your pieces lined up with the enemy king or queen, with another of your pieces in between. If the middle piece moves with a threat, your opponent can't deal with both.

u3-l03-s08.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u3-l03-s08.hint: Move the piece that's blocking another of yours: that way you attack two things at once.

u3-l03-s09.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.

u3-l04-s01.text: In a double check, two pieces give check at once. You can't block both or capture both: the only option is to move the king. Here the black queen could capture the knight, but the rook's check would remain.

u3-l04-s02.prompt: Give double check with the knight and the bishop.
u3-l04-s02.hint: If the knight leaves the bishop's diagonal with check, that's two checks at once.
u3-l04-s02.success: Correct. The knight gives check and uncovers the bishop's check: the king has to move.

u3-l04-s03.hint: The knight can give check and uncover the rook's check. The king is surrounded by its own pieces.
u3-l04-s03.success: Correct. Double check and mate: the king has nowhere to go.

u3-l04-s04.text: The queen is an expert at double attacks: it can attack two loose pieces at once, on different lines.

u3-l04-s05.prompt: Give check with the queen and attack the rook at the same time.
u3-l04-s05.hint: Look for a check on the king's diagonal that also points at the rook on a2.
u3-l04-s05.success: Correct. Check and an attack on the rook: after the check, you capture it.

u3-l04-s06.prompt: Attack the knight and the bishop at once, since both are loose.
u3-l04-s06.hint: The knight and the bishop are on the same rank: get onto that rank.
u3-l04-s06.success: Correct. The queen attacks both pieces: only one can be saved.

u3-l04-s07.prompt: Why is double check so strong?
options: The only answer is to move the king
u3-l04-s07.explanation: With two checks at once, blocking or capturing one piece isn't enough: the king has to move.
feedback: It isn't always mate: sometimes the king has a free square.
That depends on the position: what's certain is that the king has to move.

u3-l04-s08.hint: Look for a move where two pieces give check at once.

u3-l05.title: Remove the defender
u3-l05.summary: Capture the piece doing the defending

u3-l05-s01.text: If one piece defends another, capture or trade the defender: the other piece is left unprotected. Here the knight on f6 defends the rook on d5. If you capture it with check, there's no time to save the rook.

u3-l05-s02.prompt: Tap the black piece that defends the rook on d5.
u3-l05-s02.hint: Look for the black piece that could recapture on d5.

u3-l05-s03.prompt: Remove the defender with check and win the rook.
u3-l05-s03.success: Correct. Bxf6+ and, after Kxf6, Nxd5+: the rook had lost its defender.
u3-l05-s03.hint: First capture the piece that defends the rook.

u3-l05-s04.prompt: Trade off the defender of the bishop on b4 and win it.
u3-l05-s04.success: Correct. You traded your bishop for the knight and won the bishop on b4.
u3-l05-s04.hint: The knight on c6 defends the bishop: your bishop can capture it.

u3-l05-s05.prompt: The knight on f6 defends h7. Remove it and threaten mate.
u3-l05-s05.hint: Your queen and knight attack h7. Apart from the king, only the knight on f6 defends it.
u3-l05-s05.success: Correct. Without the knight, Qxh7 is mate.

u3-l05-s06.explanation: Nxd5 Nxd5 trades the rook for a knight. Bxf6+ first wins the whole rook: the defender is gone.
feedback: Nxd5 wins something, but the knight on f6 recaptures. Remove the defender first.

u3-l05-s07.text: Before attacking a piece, check who defends it. If you can capture or trade the defender, the piece is left hanging.

u3-l05-s08.prompt: Remove the defender and win material.
u3-l05-s08.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u3-l05-s08.hint: Find which piece defends another and capture it or trade it.

u3-l06.title: Deflection
u3-l06.summary: Pull the defender out of position

u3-l06-s01.text: A deflection forces a piece to stop defending a square. Here the rook on d8 defends the queen and the back rank. If the white queen captures, the rook has to recapture and leaves e8 unguarded.

u3-l06-s02.prompt: Tap the black piece that has two jobs at once.
u3-l06-s02.hint: One piece defends the queen and also the square e8.

u3-l06-s03.prompt: Deflect the rook that defends the back rank and deliver mate.
u3-l06-s03.success: Correct. The rook had to recapture and Re8 was mate.
u3-l06-s03.hint: The rook on c8 defends the bishop and the back rank. Capture the bishop.

u3-l06-s04.prompt: Give check with the queen: the rook has to capture it and the back rank is left undefended.
u3-l06-s04.success: Correct. Qe8+ forces the rook to capture and Rxe8 is mate.
u3-l06-s04.hint: Look for a queen check on e8: your rook also points at that square.

u3-l06-s05.prompt: The black king defends the bishop on d8. Give check with the pawn to deflect it and win the bishop.
u3-l06-s05.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u3-l06-s05.hint: A pawn check forces the king to move, and every square takes it away from the bishop.

u3-l06-s06.explanation: The rook on c8 defends the bishop and also the back rank: it can't do both.
feedback: The bishop isn't defending anything important: the rook defends it.
The king can't get past its pawns, but it isn't defending anything.

u3-l06-s07.text: A piece that defends two things at once is overloaded. If you force it to deal with one, the other is left undefended.

u3-l06-s08.success: Well solved: this position comes from a real game.
u3-l06-s08.hint: Force an enemy piece to stop defending a square, usually with a check.

u3-l07-s01.text: In a back-rank mate, the king is shut in on the back rank by its own pawns, and a rook or the queen delivers mate.

u3-l07-s02.hint: The black king can't get off the back rank.

u3-l07-s03.prompt: You're playing Black. Deliver a back-rank mate.
u3-l07-s03.hint: The white king is shut in by its pawns.

u3-l07-s04.text: To avoid it, give your king an exit: a pawn move like h3 frees up h2. Having a rook guard the back rank works too.

u3-l07-s05.prompt: Black threatens Rd1 mate. Which move stops it?
u3-l07-s05.explanation: With h3, the king has the square h2 to escape to: Rd1+ is no longer mate.
feedback: a3 doesn't give the king an exit.
b4 doesn't give the king an exit.

u3-l07-s06.text: Scholar's Mate: the queen and bishop team up on f7, the weak square defended only by the king. If Black doesn't see it, Qxf7 is mate.

u3-l07-s07.prompt: You're playing Black. The queen and bishop threaten Qxf7 mate. Defend yourself.
u3-l07-s07.hint: Defend f7 with your queen or knight, or attack the white queen with a pawn.
u3-l07-s07.success: Correct. There's no more mate on f7.

u3-l07-s08.prompt: Which square do the white queen and bishop attack together?
u3-l07-s08.explanation: f7: the queen on h5 and the bishop on c4 attack it, and only the king defends it.
feedback: e5 is attacked only by the queen.
h7 is attacked only by the queen, and the rook defends it.

u3-l07-s09.hint: The king is shut in on the back rank by its own pawns.

u3-l08.title: Before you move: checks, captures and threats
u3-l08.summary: The routine that keeps your pieces safe

u3-l08-s01.text: Before each move, follow a routine: first, what does your opponent's last move threaten? Then, go through your checks, your captures and your threats.

u3-l08-s02.prompt: Black just played b5. Tap your piece that's now under attack.
u3-l08-s02.hint: The pawn on b5 attacks diagonally.

u3-l08-s03.prompt: Black just played Nb4. What's the threat?
options: A fork on c2: check to the king and an attack on the rook
u3-l08-s03.explanation: From c2, the knight would check the king on e1 and attack the rook on a1.
feedback: Look at where the knight can jump.
Look at where the knight can jump.

u3-l08-s04.prompt: Stop the knight fork on c2.
u3-l08-s04.hint: Cover the square c2, or move the king or the rook out of the way.
u3-l08-s04.success: Correct. The fork no longer works.

u3-l08-s05.prompt: Black left a piece undefended. Capture it.
u3-l08-s05.hint: Go through your captures: which black piece has no defender?
u3-l08-s05.success: Correct. The bishop on g4 was undefended.

u3-l08-s06.prompt: Tap all the black pieces you can capture for free.
u3-l08-s06.hint: Look for black pieces that your pieces attack and that nothing defends.

u3-l08-s07.text: The tactics in this unit can be used against you too. Going through checks, captures and threats before you move helps you see them coming.
